steps.prompt: New quest: read {quest} (and the code it cites; the MuJoCo API is node_modules/@mujoco/mujoco/mujoco.d.ts). Write the spec to {run}/spec.md following your role card: the new species data for horse and dog (every joint: name, parent body, axis, range, sign convention), numbered test cases with hand-checked expected values (joint counts, masses before/after, the kinematic splay check, the existing real-MuJoCo checks, and the stand-hold measurement with the numbers you ran in your scratchpad, including the smallest :kp that holds if today's doesn't), and a who-touches-what table. Reply when it's written.

prompt.un-automate-monde: Spec: {run}/spec.md (quest: {quest}). Implement it in the source and data files the spec assigns the builder, regenerate creatures/bodies/*.xml with bb creature-mjcf (never hand-edit them), and nothing else. Don't change :kp unless the spec says Michael decided it. Run .crew/gate.sh before replying.
prompt.le-testeur: Spec: {run}/spec.md (quest: {quest}). Write its test cases in the test file(s) the spec assigns the tester, and nothing else, including the real-MuJoCo Node test (load MuJoCo with js/require as test/pm/creature_mujoco_test.cljs does). The builder is coding in parallel.

steps.prompt: Run the gate (.crew/gate.sh) and write the gate note to {run}/gate-note.md as your role card says.

Review the round's changes against {run}/spec.md and {quest}: git diff for edited files, and read the new files (git status lists them). Check: 18 joints per species with the spec's axes, ranges and signs; the root body is still :torso; nothing reads joints by a fixed count or a species name; the generated XMLs come from bb creature-mjcf; the old real-MuJoCo checks still run unchanged in intent; the stand-hold measurement is real and reported, and :kp wasn't silently raised. Write the review to {run}/review.md (at most 5 ranked findings).
